name: BigBird (global+window+random)
tagline: Block-sparse attention pattern combining global tokens, a local window, and per-block random keys to hit a fixed density budget.
pseudocode:
1. Partition keys into blocks of $B = 64$
2. Mark first $g = 2$ blocks as GLOBAL (attended-by and attended-to all)
3. Add WINDOW: $|b_i - b_j| \le w/2$ with $w = 3$ blocks (band)
4. Pick $r$ extra RANDOM blocks per query block to fit budget: $r = \max(0, \mathrm{round}(0.88\cdot\rho\cdot n_b) - g - w)$
5. AND with causal mask if causal
6. Token-level softmax-attention with $-\infty$ on dropped pairs
diff_from_baseline: Zaheer et al., NeurIPS 2020 ('Big Bird: Transformers for Longer Sequences'). Static fixed pattern that satisfies the density constraint without per-query content scoring.

name: Block Top-K (NSA-style)
tagline: Score key blocks by mean-pooled q-k dot product per query block; keep the top-K block columns plus the diagonal block.
pseudocode:
1. Pad N to multiple of $B$ blocks; mean-pool $q$ and $k$ per block
2. scores $= q_{\text{blk}} k_{\text{blk}}^\top \cdot s$ (mask non-causal pairs)
3. Solve K from causal density quadratic: $K(2n_b+1-K) = \rho\,n_b(n_b+1)$
4. For each query block, pick top-(K-1) key blocks by score and force-include diagonal
5. Expand block keep -> token-level mask, AND with causal
6. Softmax-attend over kept positions only
diff_from_baseline: NSA-style mean-pooled block selection; content-adaptive analogue of FlexPrefill that works without a decode-time KV cache.

name: Dense oracle
tagline: Standard dense causal attention — upper-bound quality reference; only allowed to exceed the density budget via ALLOW_DENSE_FLAG.
diff_from_baseline: Vaswani et al. 2017 dense attention. Oracle baseline that bypasses the harness density budget for quality reference.

name: StreamingLLM (sinks + window)
tagline: Each query attends to the first num_sinks 'attention sink' tokens plus a sliding causal window of size W solved analytically from the budget.
pseudocode:
1. Causal: solve $W = \mathrm{round}(\rho(N+1)/2) - s$ where $s$=sinks
2. Non-causal: $W = (\mathrm{round}(\rho N) - s - 1)/2$
3. Build mask = (recent-window) OR (column $< s$)
4. AND with causal lower triangle if causal
5. Softmax over kept positions; report measured density
diff_from_baseline: Xiao et al., ICLR 2024 ('Efficient Streaming Language Models with Attention Sinks', arXiv:2309.17453). Sinks + sliding-window pattern that recovers most dense quality on streaming inputs.

name: FlexPrefill
tagline: Adaptive content-aware block-sparse prefill that picks important key blocks per query block during long-context prefill.
pseudocode:
1. Partition Q into query blocks; pool/representative-vector per block
2. Score K blocks vs each Q block with low-rank approx
3. Pick top-$\lceil \rho\,n_b \rceil$ key blocks per query block
4. Keep diagonal + sink/causal constraints; build token mask
5. Softmax-attend only on kept blocks
diff_from_baseline: Lai et al., 2024 (FlexPrefill, arXiv:2502.20766). Adaptive sparse-attention prefill; representative content-aware baseline for long-context inference.

name: H2O (heavy hitters)
tagline: Keeps a small set of 'heavy hitter' KV positions whose accumulated attention weights are largest, plus a recent window.
pseudocode:
1. Maintain running sum of attention probabilities per key position
2. At each step, designate the top-$h$ accumulated-attention positions as heavy hitters
3. Always attend to: heavy hitters $\cup$ last-$w$ recent tokens
4. AND with causal mask
5. Compute attention only over the union
diff_from_baseline: Zhang et al., NeurIPS 2023 ('H2O: Heavy-Hitter Oracle for Efficient Generative Inference of LLMs', arXiv:2306.14048). Decode-time KV-eviction policy adapted to a parallel-prefill density mask.

name: SnapKV
tagline: Selects KV positions to keep based on the attention an observation window of recent queries pays to past keys, then attends only to the snapshot.
pseudocode:
1. Pick observation window: last $w$ queries
2. Aggregate attention scores from those queries onto all past keys
3. Select top-$k$ key positions by aggregated score (plus a recent window)
4. Keep the selected KV positions, drop the rest
5. Compute attention only on the snapshot under causal mask
diff_from_baseline: Li et al., NeurIPS 2024 ('SnapKV: LLM Knows What You Are Looking for Before Generation', arXiv:2404.14469). Observation-window KV compression baseline applied here as a sparse-attention mask.
